extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers (novelists and memoirists) seeking craft advice on endings
extracted.subtask_description: Practical craft guidelines for writing a satisfying final chapter for a novel or memoir: genre-specific expectations, structural aims (resolution after climax), tone and line-level advice (final line, avoiding deus ex machina), and series/serial considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final chapter is dictated by genre
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventions in fiction endings tend to spring from the two classic forms of fiction: comedy and tragedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the genre's expectations before designing the ending: comedies tend toward communal/feast endings (weddings, parties), tragedies toward death/resolution. Use the genre frame to decide what kind of closure readers expect; deviations are possible but risk making readers feel cheated unless handled carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Romance: Happy Ever After (HEA) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Romance requires that Happy Ever After (HEA) ending in the final chapter, preferably with a wedding or a betrothal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If aiming for modern HEA, a gathering, toasts, or a kiss-and-fade-to-black can suffice. Ensure the central romantic arc is resolved convincingly — readers of romance expect a satisfying relationship conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mystery: reveal the culprit and tie up subplots
rubrics_metrics.description: You need a modern equivalent that concludes with the discovery of the murderer, then the detective and friends retire to a pub or cafe to tie up the subplots — a form of the classic comedy 'feast' ending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mystery's central question must be answered; follow-up scenes should close or explain remaining threads so readers feel the investigation is complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary fiction: freedom but avoid cheating the reader
rubrics_metrics.description: You get to do whatever you like with your final chapter if you’re a literary author. But don’t do something that will make your reader feel cheated or angry. If you kill off a major character, make sure readers are prepared for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise freedom responsibly: unexpected or unconventional endings are allowed but must be earned by the text (foreshadowing, thematic setup) to avoid alienating readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thrillers: preserve larger-stakes stability
rubrics_metrics.description: Thrillers need to end with the world not getting blown up by the evil mastermind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolve the high-stakes threat so readers sense the danger has been averted; even if costs are high, the core catastrophe should be prevented or addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic suspense: deliver an 'ah-ha' twist, not a 'WTF'
rubrics_metrics.description: You want a twist, but it needs to be an 'ah-ha' moment, not a 'WTF?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surprises should feel earned and retrospectively obvious — provide clues so readers can look back and say they should have seen it coming rather than feeling blindsided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epic fantasy ending conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Epic Fantasy often ends with a detached historical overview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider a wrap-up that places events in a larger historical context (an epilogue-as-history) when appropriate for epic scope; this can create distance and sense of lasting consequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: MG/YA and other fantasy: homecoming plus wistful hook
rubrics_metrics.description: Other fantasies—especially MG or YA—will end with the protagonist safely home from the adventure, but perhaps a bit wistful, hoping for more adventures in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Close the immediate adventure and emotional arc while leaving room for future quests or growth; a hopeful/bittersweet tone often works well for younger-audience fantasies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure the story builds to a climax and true conclusion (avoid episodic structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many 'novels' that feel endless are actually a series of episodes that don't build to a climax or a resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the narrative so episodes contribute to escalating stakes and lead to a real climax and denouement; if the work feels like a collection of scenes, rework or remove material that doesn't advance toward the ending.

rubrics_metrics.name: It's acceptable to write the final chapter early
rubrics_metrics.description: It's okay to write your final chapter before the book is complete; picturing the ending and jotting notes (sometimes a final sentence) can give direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an early-final-chapter draft as a guiding goal; expect to rewrite it as the story evolves, but having an endpoint can prevent tangent-filled middles and help maintain focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final chapter should give readers resolution after the climax
rubrics_metrics.description: The final chapter is a kind of closing argument, where you can show your themes and show what your characters have learned from this experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide emotional and thematic closure: demonstrate character growth, answer the major questions raised by the plot, and connect the ending back to the inciting incident or the book's beginnings when possible. Avoid ending on a raw action beat with no closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not leave readers hanging on a cliff (resolve major arcs)
rubrics_metrics.description: You need to wrap up all the major loose ends of this book. Leaving the reader hanging is bad manners and will anger readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolve the central arcs of the book; if writing a series, you may leave a single minor hook for the next installment but avoid withholding the primary resolutions to force purchases. Follow examples like The Hunger Games where the first book wraps its story but still leads onto the next book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the final line memorably and thematically
rubrics_metrics.description: A memorable final line can sell your next book. If you can tie that line back to the beginning of the story, or echo the title, it feels especially satisfying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft a final line that resonates with theme, character change, or the opening material — it should linger and ideally refract the whole book in a single, telling image or turn of phrase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid deus ex machina and unforeshadowed off-the-wall twists
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid that Deus Ex Machina or Off-the-Wall 'Twist' in the Final Chapter. Telling us it was all a dream, or a story your protagonist is writing, is bound to bring disappointment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you include a surprising resolution, ensure the necessary elements are present earlier in the narrative so the twist feels earned. Do not introduce entirely new, unmotivated devices (aliens, time travel, etc.) solely to rescue or upend the plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave the reader wanting more — avoid overlong epilogues
rubrics_metrics.description: Leave some things to the reader’s imagination; don’t stay too long at the party. Ambiguity is okay as long as you are not withholding vital information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trim extraneous 'where-are-they-now' chatter and resist over-explaining. End with enough detail for satisfaction but not so much that the ending becomes tedious; a concise, evocative close encourages readers to ponder rather than be overloaded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match the ending’s tone to the rest of the book
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting the right tone for the ending is tough. We want to end on a positive note, but it has to stay in keeping with the tone of the rest of the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure emotional register, voice, and stylistic tone in the final chapter are consistent with what precedes it; abrupt tonal shifts can undermine reader satisfaction even if plot points are resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewrite and polish the final chapter repeatedly to capture tone and resonance
rubrics_metrics.description: Rewriting the last scene many times helps capture the right tone and resonance; it often includes one last surprise and personal epiphanies for the lead characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the final chapter as a high-value scene: iterate on sentence-level choices, pacing, and emotional beats; aim for an ending that produces an 'Ah!' of recognition and satisfaction in readers.
